questions.q: Who typically makes the final go/no-go decision for go-live, and on what basis?
options: A random vote among all business users
The steering committee, based on the cutover validation results
Oracle Support, based on a Service Request
The Technical Consultant alone, based on personal confidence
questions.explain: The final go/no-go decision is typically made by a steering committee (sponsor, project managers, solution architect) based directly on cutover validation results.

questions.q: What is a "command center" (or war room) used for after go-live?
options: Real-time issue triage by the implementation team as business users transact live for the first time
Storing the configuration workbook
Running the final UAT sign-off meeting
Hosting the project kickoff workshop
questions.explain: The command center is where consultants are available in real time to triage issues as business users begin using the live system.

questions.q: Who is often the first line of support for colleagues immediately after go-live, before escalating further?
options: The Executive Sponsor
Oracle Support via a Service Request
Super users
The external auditor
questions.explain: Super users, selected and trained earlier in the project, are often the first point of contact for colleagues, escalating to the command center only when needed.

questions.q: Why does something almost always surface during go-live even after thorough testing?
options: Because testing is pointless and should be skipped
Because real production volume and real user behavior inevitably include scenarios no script anticipated
Because Oracle intentionally breaks systems at go-live
Because the cutover plan is never actually followed
questions.explain: Even a well-tested go-live surfaces new edge cases from real users and real transaction volume — an expected reality, not evidence that testing failed.

questions.q: What happened during Brightfield's day-one go-live support?
options: The system failed completely and cutover was rolled back
The steering committee withheld the go decision
No issues were reported at all
Eleven issues were logged, mostly minor navigation questions plus one configuration fix resolved within hours
questions.explain: Brightfield's command center handled eleven day-one issues — mostly navigation questions resolved by super users, plus one real configuration fix completed quickly.
